layerStatement.resolution: the package is RESOLVED BY ITS PUBLISHED NAME through scratch/node_modules/provident-storeroom -> bindings/js (package.json v0.1.3, exports "." -> ./index.mjs); the kernel module is reached at its declared checkout home bindings/js/src/constraint-kernel.mjs, whose own fixture binding is the package SELF-REFERENCE (Node resolves 'provident-storeroom' from bindings/js/src to bindings/js/index.mjs), so the kernel, the driver and the store share ONE module instance and ONE loaded addon; the Rust store behind the JS binding is exercised in a real Node process (node v24.20.0).
layerStatement.publishedInstall: NOT exercised, and it could not show this demo at all: package.json "files" carries index.mjs + README.md + index.d.ts only and "exports" declares "." alone, so an install from the registry carries NO src/constraint-kernel.mjs and no subpath that reaches it — the constraint kernel is checkout-only (kernel-surface.md §1 item 1). `settle` IS a member of the published instance (it is built by storeCreate in index.mjs), so a published install WOULD show the fourth member and the withheld post-verb window for a write an install's own code adopted — but it could not show the constraint pass, its ordering, its discard, or the kernel's two settle instants, because no consumer can reach src/.
layerStatement.settleWrapper: the instance's `settle` member is wrapped by this driver ON THE INSTANCE IT ITSELF CREATED, for the trail alone (it records the reach, the phase and the pending length, then calls the original member with the same receiver and same argument). No package file, no kernel module and no existing record was edited.
